chunks: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم stood at ʿArafah on the left side of the mountain. The people began hurrying toward the hoofprints of his she-camel and stood beside it, so he moved it away, but they did the same again. He said: “O people, the place beneath the hooves of my she-camel is not itself the standing place; rather, all of this is a standing place.” He gestured with his hand and said عليه السلام: “All of ʿArafah is a standing place, and if there were nothing except what was beneath the hoof of my she-camel, that would not suffice for the people.”

And he عليه السلام did likewise in al-Muzdalifah. So when you see an open space, move forward and fill it with yourself and your mount, for Allah, the Exalted, loves that those gaps be filled. Move away from the hills, and avoid al-Arāk, Namirah—which is the valley floor of ʿUranah—Thawiyyah, and Dhā al-Majāz, for they are not part of ʿArafāt.

key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَةِ: Muzdalifah, where the pilgrims also perform wuquf
key_terms.الْهِضَابِ: the hills or elevated ground to move away from
key_terms.خَلَلًا: an open gap or empty space within the standing area
key_terms.ذَا الْمَجَازِ: Dhā al-Majāz, a place stated not to be part of ʿArafāt
key_terms.عَرَفَةُ: ʿArafah, the site of standing during hajj
key_terms.عُرَنَةَ: ʿUranah, the valley area identified as outside ʿArafāt
key_terms.مَوْقِفٌ: the place of standing for the hajj rite
key_terms.نَمِرَةَ: Namirah, a location excluded from ʿArafāt in this context

ai.seo_question: Is the standing place in ʿArafah limited to the exact spot where the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم stood?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the mawqif at ʿArafah and al-Muzdalifah is not restricted to the exact place where the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم stood; rather, the designated area as a whole is valid for wuquf. It also identifies places to avoid because they are outside the legal boundary of ʿArafāt, making the narration important for hajj rulings.
